searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he generation 4 — gevurah risk map the awtsmoos gives expansion a boundary so light does not shatter its vessel; awtsmoos.com must move quickly, yet every release step must remain exact, reversible, and level. highest risk failure modes 1. deploying untested local code because the dirty canonical checkout is behind origin/main. 2. overwriting unrelated concurrent agent work while trying to fast forward main. 3. shipping a stale tunnel manifest that omits newly added runtime modules. 4. treating a 120 url sample as proof of the entire 603 url discovery graph. 5. following redirects silently and thereby hiding bad sitemap/canonical urls. 6. weakening the crawler to make a failure disappear instead of fixing discovery. 7. treating missing post semantic markers as indexable content rather than checking robots/schema semantics. 8. assuming old 8941/8943 process caches reflect final clean worktree code. 9. pushing after origin/main moved without transplanting/retesting on the new tip. 10. claiming deployment before raw public https proves the exact behavior. 11. editing generated artifacts by hand instead of rebuilding from generators. 12. editing manifest by hand instead of using the repository native manifest generator. 13. staging unrelated dirty files from the shared checkout. 14. leaving planning/evidence memory stale after implementation changes. 15. inventing titles, dates, hreflang, ratings, or other seo claims unsupported by source data. release doctrine read reality before every mutation. whole file writes only for human authored source. generated artifacts only through their generators. keep source modules <=120 lines and tab indented. heavy compatibility suites run serially; independent read only diagnostics may run concurrently. integration happens in a clean current origin worktree, not by forcing the dirty canonical checkout. production activation is exact sha, followed by raw public acceptance.
